text: pushout glues two ACSets along common substructure. Given morphisms f:→Bf: \B g:→Cg: \C, pushout identifies f()f() g()g() part aa AA.
code: # Glue two edges at a shared vertex A <- Graph(); add_vertices(A, 1)  # Shared vertex #> [1] 1 B <- path_graph(2)                 # 1 → 2 C <- path_graph(2)                 # 1 → 2  # Share the source vertex f <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = 1L, E = integer(0)), A, B) g <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = 1L, E = integer(0)), A, C)  po <- pushout(f, g) cat("Pushout: V =", nv(po$pushout), ", E =", ne(po$pushout), "\n") #> Pushout: V = 3 , E = 2 # 2 + 2 - 1 = 3 vertices, 2 edges (the shared vertex is identified)

title: Limits, colimits, and graph rewriting in catlab
text: pullback cospan B→D←CB \D \leftarrow C consists pairs (b,c)(b, c) f(b)=g(c)f(b) = g(c) — “fiber product.”
code: # D: 2 vertices; B: 3 vertices mapping {1,2→1, 3→2}; C: 2 vertices mapping {1→1, 2→2} D <- Graph(); add_vertices(D, 2) #> [1] 1 2 B <- Graph(); add_vertices(B, 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 C <- Graph(); add_vertices(C, 2) #> [1] 1 2  f <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), B, D) g <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), C, D)  pb <- pullback(f, g) cat("Pullback: V =", nv(pb$pullback), "\n") #> Pullback: V = 3 cat("Pairs (B, C):") #> Pairs (B, C): for (i in seq_len(nv(pb$pullback))) {   cat(sprintf(" (%d,%d)", pb$proj1@components$V[i], pb$proj2@components$V[i])) } #>  (1,1) (2,1) (3,2) cat("\n") # Fiber over D=1: B parts {1,2} × C parts {1} = 2 pairs # Fiber over D=2: B parts {3} × C parts {2} = 1 pair

title: Limits, colimits, and graph rewriting in catlab
text: Create rule adds edge two matched vertices.
code: # Interface: 2 isolated vertices I <- Graph(); add_vertices(I, 2) #> [1] 1 2 # Pattern: 2 isolated vertices (same as interface) L <- Graph(); add_vertices(L, 2) #> [1] 1 2 # Replacement: edge 1 → 2 R <- path_graph(2)  l <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), I, L) r <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), I, R) add_edge_rule <- rule(l, r)  # Apply to a graph with 3 isolated vertices G <- Graph(); add_vertices(G, 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 H <- rewrite(add_edge_rule, G) cat("Before: V =", nv(G), ", E =", ne(G), "\n") #> Before: V = 3 , E = 0 cat("After:  V =", nv(H), ", E =", ne(H), "\n") #> After:  V = 3 , E = 1

code: # Try to delete a vertex from a graph where it has edges I <- Graph() L <- Graph(); add_vertices(L, 1) #> [1] 1 R <- Graph()  l <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = integer(0), E = integer(0)), I, L) r <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = integer(0), E = integer(0)), I, R) del_vertex_rule <- rule(l, r, monic = FALSE)  G <- path_graph(2)  # 1 → 2 # Matching vertex 1 (which has an outgoing edge) should fail tryCatch(   rewrite_match(del_vertex_rule,     ACSetTransformation(list(V = 1L, E = integer(0)), L, G)),   error = function(e) cat("Expected error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n") ) #> Expected error: Gluing condition violated: dangling edge #> ℹ Part 1 of E maps via src to deleted part 1 of V

title: Limits, colimits, and graph rewriting in catlab
text: Given functor F:C→DF: C \D DD-set, delta migration produces CC-set pulling back along FF.
code: # Reverse a graph: swap src and tgt cat_G <- FinCat(schema = SchGraph) reverse_F <- FinFunctor(   ob_map = list(V = "V", E = "E"),   hom_map = list(src = "tgt", tgt = "src"),  # Swap!   dom = cat_G, codom = cat_G )  g <- path_graph(3)  # 1 → 2 → 3 GraphType <- acset_type(SchGraph) g_rev <- delta_migrate(reverse_F, g, GraphType)  cat("Original: src =", subpart(g, NULL, "src"), ", tgt =", subpart(g, NULL, "tgt"), "\n") #> Original: src = 1 2 , tgt = 2 3 cat("Reversed: src =", subpart(g_rev, NULL, "src"), ", tgt =", subpart(g_rev, NULL, "tgt"), "\n") #> Reversed: src = 2 3 , tgt = 1 2

title: Limits, colimits, and graph rewriting in catlab
text: Sigma migration left adjoint delta — pushes data forward along functor via colimits.
code:
# Combine two edge types into one graph dom_sch <- BasicSchema(   obs = c("V", "E1", "E2"),   homs = list(     hom("src1", "E1", "V"), hom("tgt1", "E1", "V"),     hom("src2", "E2", "V"), hom("tgt2", "E2", "V")   ) ) codom_sch <- BasicSchema(   obs = c("V", "E"),   homs = list(hom("src", "E", "V"), hom("tgt", "E", "V")) )  cat_dom <- FinCat(schema = dom_sch) cat_codom <- FinCat(schema = codom_sch) F <- FinFunctor(   ob_map = list(V = "V", E1 = "E", E2 = "E"),   hom_map = list(src1 = "src", tgt1 = "tgt", src2 = "src", tgt2 = "tgt"),   dom = cat_dom, codom = cat_codom )  # Source: 3 vertices, 1 E1-edge (1→2), 1 E2-edge (2→3) source <- ACSet(dom_sch) add_parts(source, "V", 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 add_parts(source, "E1", 1) #> [1] 1 set_subpart(source, 1, "src1", 1); set_subpart(source, 1, "tgt1", 2) add_parts(source, "E2", 1) #> [1] 1 set_subpart(source, 1, "src2", 2); set_subpart(source, 1, "tgt2", 3)  ResultType <- acset_type(codom_sch) result <- sigma_migrate(F, source, ResultType) cat("Combined graph: V =", nparts(result, "V"), ", E =", nparts(result, "E"), "
") #> Combined graph: V = 3 , E = 2 cat("Edge sources:", subpart(result, NULL, "src"), "
") #> Edge sources: 1 2 cat("Edge targets:", subpart(result, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #> Edge targets: 2 3

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: applied category theory, schema small category describes shape data — types entities relationships . database instance (dataset) schema 𝒞\mathcal{C} set-valued functor X:𝒞→𝐒𝐞𝐭X : \mathcal{C} \\mathbf{Set}, assigning set rows entity type function relationship. catlab package, schemas represented BasicSchema objects instances ACSets (attributed C-sets). schema morphism — functor F:𝒞→𝒟F : \mathcal{C} \\mathcal{D} schemas — induces data migration functors systematically transform data one schema another: Delta migration (ΔF\Delta_F): pulls data back along FF (pullback / precomposition) Sigma migration (ΣF\Sigma_F): pushes data forward along FF (left Kan extension) operations adjoint: ΣF⊣ΔF\Sigma_F \dashv \Delta_F. Together provide principled, compositional framework data transformation goes far beyond ad-hoc ETL scripts.
code: library(catlab) library(acsets) #>  #> Attaching package: 'acsets' #> The following object is masked from 'package:graphics': #>  #>     arrows #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     objects

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: BasicSchema declares objects (entity types), homs (foreign keys), optionally attribute types attributes. Wrapping schema FinCat() treats finite category; FinFunctor() creates structure-preserving map two categories. functor F:𝒞→𝒟F : \mathcal{C} \\mathcal{D} specified : ob_map: named list sending object 𝒞\mathcal{C} object 𝒟\mathcal{D} hom_map: named list sending hom (attribute) 𝒞\mathcal{C} hom (attribute) 𝒟\mathcal{D} functor must preserve source/target structure morphisms.
code:
# The standard directed-graph schema SchGraph #> <acsets::BasicSchema> #>  @ obs      : chr [1:2] "V" "E" #>  @ homs     :List of 2 #>  .. $ :List of 3 #>  ..  ..$ name : chr "src" #>  ..  ..$ dom  : chr "E" #>  ..  ..$ codom: chr "V" #>  .. $ :List of 3 #>  ..  ..$ name : chr "tgt" #>  ..  ..$ dom  : chr "E" #>  ..  ..$ codom: chr "V" #>  @ attrtypes: chr(0)  #>  @ attrs    : list() cat("Objects:", objects(SchGraph), "
") #> Objects: V E cat("Homs:
") #> Homs: for (h in homs(SchGraph)) {   cat(sprintf("  %s : %s -> %s
", h$name, h$dom, h$codom)) } #>   src : E -> V #>   tgt : E -> V

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Given functor F:𝒞→𝒟F : \mathcal{C} \\mathcal{D} 𝒟\mathcal{D}-set XX, delta migration ΔF(X)\Delta_F(X) 𝒞\mathcal{C}-set defined precomposition: ΔF(X)=X∘F\Delta_F(X) = X \circ F. Concretely: object cc 𝒞\mathcal{C}, set parts ΔF(X)(c)=X(F(c))\Delta_F(X)(c) = X(F(c)) hom h:c1→c2h : c_1 \c_2 𝒞\mathcal{C}, function ΔF(X)(h)=X(F(h))\Delta_F(X)(h) = X(F(h)) Delta migration intuitive operation: renames reorganises data reinterpreting underlying tables different lens.

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: simplest non-trivial delta migration swaps src tgt homs graph, reversing every edge. reversed path graph vertices edges, every arrow points opposite direction: 4→3→2→14 \3 \2 \1.
code:
# Functor F : SchGraph → SchGraph that swaps src and tgt cat_G <- FinCat(schema = SchGraph) F_rev <- FinFunctor(   ob_map  = list(V = "V", E = "E"),   hom_map = list(src = "tgt", tgt = "src"),   dom = cat_G, codom = cat_G )  g <- path_graph(4)  # 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 cat("Original graph:
") #> Original graph: cat("  src:", subpart(g, NULL, "src"), "
") #>   src: 1 2 3 cat("  tgt:", subpart(g, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #>   tgt: 2 3 4  GraphType <- acset_type(SchGraph) g_rev <- delta_migrate(F_rev, g, GraphType) cat("
Reversed graph (delta along F_rev):
") #>  #> Reversed graph (delta along F_rev): cat("  src:", subpart(g_rev, NULL, "src"), "
") #>   src: 2 3 4 cat("  tgt:", subpart(g_rev, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #>   tgt: 1 2 3 cat("Original DOT:
") #> Original DOT: cat(to_dot(g)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #>   4; #>   1 -> 2; #>   2 -> 3; #>   3 -> 4; #> } cat("
Reversed DOT:
") #>  #> Reversed DOT: cat(to_dot(g_rev)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #>   4; #>   2 -> 1; #>   3 -> 2; #>   4 -> 3; #> }

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Delta migration can project richer schema onto simpler one. Consider weighted graph — can forget weights pulling back along inclusion SchGraph SchWeightedGraph. structure (vertices, edges, source/target) preserved exactly; weight attribute — preimage FF — discarded.
code:
# Functor embedding SchGraph into SchWeightedGraph cat_plain <- FinCat(schema = SchGraph) cat_wt    <- FinCat(schema = SchWeightedGraph)  F_incl <- FinFunctor(   ob_map  = list(V = "V", E = "E"),   hom_map = list(src = "src", tgt = "tgt"),   dom = cat_plain, codom = cat_wt )  # A weighted graph: triangle with weights wg <- WeightedGraph(   V = 3, E = 3,   src = c(1L, 2L, 3L), tgt = c(2L, 3L, 1L),   weight = c(1.0, 2.5, 0.7) ) cat("Weighted graph: V =", nparts(wg, "V"), ", E =", nparts(wg, "E"), "
") #> Weighted graph: V = 3 , E = 3 cat("  weights:", subpart(wg, NULL, "weight"), "
") #>   weights: 1 2.5 0.7  # Delta pulls back to a plain graph — weights are dropped plain <- delta_migrate(F_incl, wg, GraphType) cat("
Plain graph (delta forgets weights):
") #>  #> Plain graph (delta forgets weights): cat("  V =", nparts(plain, "V"), ", E =", nparts(plain, "E"), "
") #>   V = 3 , E = 3 cat("  src:", subpart(plain, NULL, "src"), "
") #>   src: 1 2 3 cat("  tgt:", subpart(plain, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #>   tgt: 2 3 1

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Sigma migration left adjoint delta. Given F:𝒞→𝒟F : \mathcal{C} \\mathcal{D} 𝒞\mathcal{C}-set XX, sigma migration ΣF(X)\Sigma_F(X) 𝒟\mathcal{D}-set computed left Kan extension. Concretely, object dd 𝒟\mathcal{D}: ΣF(X)(d)=∐{c∈𝒞∣F(c)=d}X(c)\Sigma_F(X)(d) = \coprod_{\{c \\mathcal{C} \mid F(c) = d\}} X(c) Parts different 𝒞\mathcal{C}-objects map 𝒟\mathcal{D}-object combined (coproduct = disjoint union). Hom values remapped part offsets. Sigma migration merges combines structure.

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Suppose model graph two kinds edges (e.g., red blue) separate object types E1E_1 E2E_2, source target homs. can merge single edge type using sigma migration. 2 red edges 1 blue edge combined 3 edges merged graph, sharing vertex set.
code:
# Domain schema: graph with two edge types SchTwoEdgeGraph <- BasicSchema(   obs = c("V", "E1", "E2"),   homs = list(     hom("src1", "E1", "V"), hom("tgt1", "E1", "V"),     hom("src2", "E2", "V"), hom("tgt2", "E2", "V")   ),   attrtypes = character(0),   attrs = list() )  # Functor merging E1 and E2 into E cat_two  <- FinCat(schema = SchTwoEdgeGraph) cat_one  <- FinCat(schema = SchGraph) F_merge <- FinFunctor(   ob_map  = list(V = "V", E1 = "E", E2 = "E"),   hom_map = list(src1 = "src", tgt1 = "tgt",                  src2 = "src", tgt2 = "tgt"),   dom = cat_two, codom = cat_one )  # Source data: 4 vertices, 2 "red" edges, 1 "blue" edge src_two <- ACSet(SchTwoEdgeGraph) add_parts(src_two, "V", 4) #> [1] 1 2 3 4 add_parts(src_two, "E1", 2) #> [1] 1 2 set_subpart(src_two, 1L, "src1", 1L); set_subpart(src_two, 1L, "tgt1", 2L) set_subpart(src_two, 2L, "src1", 2L); set_subpart(src_two, 2L, "tgt1", 3L) add_parts(src_two, "E2", 1) #> [1] 1 set_subpart(src_two, 1L, "src2", 3L); set_subpart(src_two, 1L, "tgt2", 4L)  cat("Two-edge-type graph:
") #> Two-edge-type graph: cat("  V =", nparts(src_two, "V"), "
") #>   V = 4 cat("  E1 =", nparts(src_two, "E1"),     " (src1:", subpart(src_two, NULL, "src1"),     ", tgt1:", subpart(src_two, NULL, "tgt1"), ")
") #>   E1 = 2  (src1: 1 2 , tgt1: 2 3 ) cat("  E2 =", nparts(src_two, "E2"),     " (src2:", subpart(src_two, NULL, "src2"),     ", tgt2:", subpart(src_two, NULL, "tgt2"), ")
") #>   E2 = 1  (src2: 3 , tgt2: 4 )  # Sigma merges both edge types into one merged <- sigma_migrate(F_merge, src_two, GraphType) cat("
Merged graph (sigma):
") #>  #> Merged graph (sigma): cat("  V =", nparts(merged, "V"), ", E =", nparts(merged, "E"), "
") #>   V = 4 , E = 3 cat("  src:", subpart(merged, NULL, "src"), "
") #>   src: 1 2 3 cat("  tgt:", subpart(merged, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #>   tgt: 2 3 4 cat(to_dot(merged)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #>   4; #>   1 -> 2; #>   2 -> 3; #>   3 -> 4; #> }

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Consider bipartite-like schema two vertex types (V1V_1 V2V_2) edges V1V_1 V2V_2. Sigma migration along functor sends vertex types single type VV collapses . 2 vertices V1V_1 become vertices 1–2 3 V2V_2 become vertices 3–5 result. Edge targets shifted accordingly: original target 1 V2V_2 becomes vertex 3 (= 2 + 1), etc.
code:
# Bipartite-ish schema SchBipartite <- BasicSchema(   obs = c("V1", "V2", "E"),   homs = list(     hom("src", "E", "V1"),     hom("tgt", "E", "V2")   ),   attrtypes = character(0),   attrs = list() )  # Functor collapsing V1, V2 → V cat_bip <- FinCat(schema = SchBipartite) F_collapse <- FinFunctor(   ob_map  = list(V1 = "V", V2 = "V", E = "E"),   hom_map = list(src = "src", tgt = "tgt"),   dom = cat_bip, codom = cat_one )  # Source: 2 left vertices, 3 right vertices, 3 edges bip <- ACSet(SchBipartite) add_parts(bip, "V1", 2) #> [1] 1 2 add_parts(bip, "V2", 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 add_parts(bip, "E", 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 set_subpart(bip, 1L, "src", 1L); set_subpart(bip, 1L, "tgt", 1L) set_subpart(bip, 2L, "src", 1L); set_subpart(bip, 2L, "tgt", 2L) set_subpart(bip, 3L, "src", 2L); set_subpart(bip, 3L, "tgt", 3L)  cat("Bipartite source:
") #> Bipartite source: cat("  V1 =", nparts(bip, "V1"), ", V2 =", nparts(bip, "V2"),     ", E =", nparts(bip, "E"), "
") #>   V1 = 2 , V2 = 3 , E = 3  collapsed <- sigma_migrate(F_collapse, bip, GraphType) cat("
Collapsed graph (sigma):
") #>  #> Collapsed graph (sigma): cat("  V =", nparts(collapsed, "V"), "(= 2 + 3), E =", nparts(collapsed, "E"), "
") #>   V = 5 (= 2 + 3), E = 3 cat("  src:", subpart(collapsed, NULL, "src"), "
") #>   src: 1 1 2 cat("  tgt:", subpart(collapsed, NULL, "tgt"), "
") #>   tgt: 3 4 5 cat(to_dot(collapsed)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #>   4; #>   5; #>   1 -> 3; #>   1 -> 4; #>   2 -> 5; #> }

text: common practical pattern schema evolution: existing schema changes (new fields, renamed entities, restructured relationships) data must migrated old schema new one. Functors provide principled way .

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Suppose start schema edges carry label attribute, evolve schema vertices edges carry labels. define functor old schema new schema. embedding maps old entity/relationship counterpart new schema.
code:
# Old schema: only edge labels SchOld <- BasicSchema(   obs = c("V", "E"),   homs = list(hom("src", "E", "V"), hom("tgt", "E", "V")),   attrtypes = "Label",   attrs = list(attr_spec("elabel", "E", "Label")) )  # New schema: vertex and edge labels (= SchLabelledGraph) SchNew <- SchLabelledGraph  # has vlabel and elabel  cat("Old schema attrs:
") #> Old schema attrs: for (a in attrs(SchOld)) cat(sprintf("  %s : %s -> %s
", a$name, a$dom, a$codom)) #>   elabel : E -> Label cat("New schema attrs:
") #> New schema attrs: for (a in attrs(SchNew)) cat(sprintf("  %s : %s -> %s
", a$name, a$dom, a$codom)) #>   vlabel : V -> Label #>   elabel : E -> Label cat_old <- FinCat(schema = SchOld) cat_new <- FinCat(schema = SchNew)  # Old → New: embed the old schema into the new one F_evolve <- FinFunctor(   ob_map  = list(V = "V", E = "E"),   hom_map = list(src = "src", tgt = "tgt", elabel = "elabel"),   dom = cat_old, codom = cat_new )

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Sigma migration pushes data old schema new schema. Vertex labels (didn’t exist old schema) left unset. edge labels preserved, vertices carried , new vlabel attribute NA (unset) — ready populated.
code:
# Old data OldGraphType <- acset_type(SchOld) old_data <- OldGraphType(   V = 3, E = 2,   src = c(1L, 2L), tgt = c(2L, 3L),   elabel = c("knows", "likes") ) cat("Old data: V =", nparts(old_data, "V"), ", E =", nparts(old_data, "E"), "
") #> Old data: V = 3 , E = 2 cat("  edge labels:", subpart(old_data, NULL, "elabel"), "
") #>   edge labels: knows likes  # Sigma: push forward to new schema new_data <- sigma_migrate(F_evolve, old_data, LabelledGraph) cat("
New data (sigma forward):
") #>  #> New data (sigma forward): cat("  V =", nparts(new_data, "V"), ", E =", nparts(new_data, "E"), "
") #>   V = 3 , E = 2 cat("  edge labels:", subpart(new_data, NULL, "elabel"), "
") #>   edge labels: knows likes cat("  vertex labels:", subpart(new_data, NULL, "vlabel"), "
") #>   vertex labels: NA NA NA

title: Data Migration with Functors
text: Delta migration pulls data new schema back old schema. vertex labels discarded since old schema place . illustrates adjunction informally: sigma adds structure (possibly leaving new fields empty), delta forgets structure (discarding fields without preimages).
code:

Important: port box corresponds one leg structured cospan. title: Graph Rewriting: DPO, SPO, and SqPO
text: Double Pushout (DPO) rewriting classical approach. Applying rule host graph G proceeds two steps: Pushout complement: Given l : → L match m : L → G, compute context graph K removing G everything matched L interface . Pushout: Glue K R along produce result H.

title: Graph Rewriting: DPO, SPO, and SqPO
text: Let’s create rule adds edge two existing vertices. interface 2 vertices map identically L R. L edges (match 2 isolated vertices), R one edge (create ). Apply rule graph 3 isolated vertices: rule found two isolated vertices added edge .
code: # Interface: 2 vertices (preserved) I <- Graph(); add_vertices(I, 2) #> [1] 1 2  # Pattern: 2 isolated vertices L <- Graph(); add_vertices(L, 2) #> [1] 1 2  # Replacement: 2 vertices connected by an edge (1 → 2) R <- path_graph(2)  # Morphisms: identity on vertices, no edges in interface l <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), I, L) r <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), I, R)  add_edge_rule <- rule(l, r) add_edge_rule@semantics #> [1] "DPO" G <- Graph(); add_vertices(G, 3) #> [1] 1 2 3 cat("Before:", nv(G), "vertices,", ne(G), "edges\n") #> Before: 3 vertices, 0 edges cat(graph_to_dot(G)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #> }  result <- rewrite(add_edge_rule, G) cat("After:", nv(result), "vertices,", ne(result), "edges\n") #> After: 3 vertices, 1 edges cat(graph_to_dot(result)) #> digraph G { #>   1; #>   2; #>   3; #>   1 -> 2; #> }

title: Graph Rewriting: DPO, SPO, and SqPO
text: Let’s create rule clones single vertex two copies: crucial detail V = c(1L, 1L) left leg: interface vertices map pattern vertex. signals matched vertex duplicated. Apply simple graph: Vertex 1 cloned two vertices, giving us 3 vertices total (2 original − 1 cloned + 2 copies = 3).
code: # Pattern: 1 vertex L_cl <- Graph(); add_vertices(L_cl, 1) #> [1] 1  # Interface: 2 vertices, both mapping to the same vertex in L I_cl <- Graph(); add_vertices(I_cl, 2) #> [1] 1 2  # Replacement: 2 separate vertices R_cl <- Graph(); add_vertices(R_cl, 2) #> [1] 1 2  # l maps both I vertices to vertex 1 in L (non-injective!) l_cl <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 1L), E = integer(0)), I_cl, L_cl) # r maps each I vertex to a distinct R vertex r_cl <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = c(1L, 2L), E = integer(0)), I_cl, R_cl)  clone_vertex <- rule(l_cl, r_cl, monic = FALSE, semantics = "SqPO") G_cl1 <- Graph(); add_vertices(G_cl1, 2) #> [1] 1 2 cat("Before:", nv(G_cl1), "vertices,", ne(G_cl1), "edges\n") #> Before: 2 vertices, 0 edges  m_cl1 <- ACSetTransformation(list(V = 1L, E = integer(0)), L_cl, G_cl1) result_cl1 <- rewrite_match(clone_vertex, m_cl1)  cat("After:", nv(result_cl1$result), "vertices,", ne(result_cl1$result), "edges\n") #> After: 3 vertices, 0 edges

title: catlab 0.1.0
text: Graph schemas constructors — SchGraph, SchSymmetricGraph, SchReflexiveGraph, SchWeightedGraph, SchLabelledGraph; convenience constructors Graph(), WeightedGraph(), LabelledGraph(); graph generators path_graph(), cycle_graph(), complete_graph(). Finite categories functors — FinCat, FinFunctor, ACSetTransformation S7 classes naturality checking (is_natural()), identity (id_transformation()), composition (compose_transformations()). Limits colimits ACSets — product(), pullback(), equalizer(), terminal(), to_terminal() (limits); coproduct(), pushout(), coequalizer(), initial(), from_initial() (colimits). Homomorphism search — backtracking-based find_homomorphism(), find_all_homomorphisms(), is_homomorphic() optional monic (injective) constraint. Algebraic graph rewriting — Rule / rule() DPO (double pushout), SPO (single pushout), SqPO (sesqui-pushout) semantics; rewrite(), rewrite_match(), get_matches(); supporting primitives pushout_complement(), cascading_complement(), final_pullback_complement(). Data migration — delta_migrate() (pullback migration) sigma_migrate() (left Kan extension / pushforward) along schema functors. Undirected wiring diagrams — SchUWD schema, UWD() constructor, uwd() convenience builder, relation() / box_spec() DSL. Typed ACSets — TypedACSet S7 class typed_acset(), typed_product(), typed_coproduct(), flatten_typed(), is_typed_morphism(), discrete_typed(). Structured cospans — StructuredCospan S7 class open_acset(), compose_cospans(), otimes_cospans(), oapply_cospans() composing open systems via undirected wiring diagrams. Graphviz output — graph_to_dot(), generic_to_dot(), petri_to_dot(), uwd_to_dot() DOT format; to_graphviz() interactive rendering via DiagrammeR.
